slides.texte_overlay:
How to become the friend
people go to for advice
Listen until they've finished. Most people jump in with solutions after ten seconds. Let them say everything first, the real problem usually comes at the end.
Ask what they want before advising. "Do you want my opinion or do you just need to vent?" This one question makes people trust you instantly.
Be honest, but kind. Say the hard thing gently. Friends come back to the person who tells them the truth without making them feel small.
Share what you've lived, not what you've read. "When it happened to me, this helped." Real experience is more convincing than any quote.
Know a little about a lot. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and it gives me more perspective when friends bring me their problems.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. It gives me more perspective when friends bring me their problems.

slides.texte_overlay: Keep their secrets. What a friend tells you stays with you, always. One leak and they'll never open up to you again, and they'll tell others too.
Follow up later. "How did the talk with your boss go?" Checking in shows you care about the person, not just about giving good advice.
